claims.statement: The Python test entry point `make test-py` runs `uv run pytest`, whose collection is configured in the root pyproject.toml: testpaths = libs/python, services, tools, tests/plugin-stubs, tests/conformance and scripts; asyncio_mode = "auto" with function-scoped default fixture loop; addopts = "--import-mode=importlib"; pythonpath = ["scripts"] so scripts/validate_contracts.py is importable by its test. tests/e2e is deliberately not on testpaths, so the walking skeleton never runs under plain `uv run pytest`.

`make test-java` runs `mvn -B verify` over the Maven aggregator (libs/java/agent-lib, libs/java/agent-lib-a2a, services/tlr-agent, services/inconsistency-agent), and the verify phase is itself a merge gate: the Spotless plugin runs `check` with palantirJavaFormat and removeUnusedImports, and maven-enforcer requires Maven >= 3.9 and Java >= 21 and bans dev.langchain4j, org.springframework.ai and org.bsc.langgraph4j (the Java counterpart of the framework guard).

`make lint` is the Python merge gate and runs four checks in order: `make guard` (as a Make prerequisite), `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .` and `uv run mypy libs/python` with strict = true for Python 3.13; ruff is configured with line-length 120, target-version py313, lint rules E/F/I/B/UP, and spikes/ excluded as throwaway code.

`make guard` fails the build if any *.py under libs/ or services/ contains a top-level import or from-import of langchain, langgraph, deepagents, llama_index, crewai or autogen (NFR-3); tools/, tests/ and spikes/ are out of its scope.

`make contracts` runs scripts/validate_contracts.py, which in a single pass validates the three JSON Schemas against the 2020-12 meta-schema, re-implements the conformance vector rules (stable ids, section/sentence keys, fingerprints, RFC 8785 cassette keys, event envelopes) and checks every expected value as a self-consistency check, resolves every Agent Card skill input/output $ref to an existing $defs entry, validates all OpenAPI documents with openapi-spec-validator, sanity-checks kg/schema.yaml for nodes and relationships, collects all errors before exiting, and exits 1 if any check fails; scripts/test_validate_contracts.py (on pytest testpaths) additionally asserts the repository's own contracts validate and that a corrupted schema or vector is actually reported.

`make e2e` depends on `make secrets` (deploy/gen-secrets.sh, which never overwrites existing secret files), then boots the whole stack with `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --profile stubs up -d --build --wait --wait-timeout 300`, and finally runs `SANDMAN_E2E=1 uv run pytest tests/e2e -q`.

Python unit and REST tests never touch the network: HTTP surfaces are built by create_app-style factories that accept injected transports, and tests drive them in-process with httpx.ASGITransport or stub outbound dependencies with httpx.MockTransport; A2aClient and A2aPluginClient accept an optional httpx.AsyncBaseTransport for exactly this purpose, and the orchestrator tests use a host-routing Router transport that dispatches by request host to the currently registered app so a test can simulate an agent restart by swapping apps.

sandman_agent.testing provides the shared test fakes — ScriptedLlmClient (returns queued responses/embeddings in order, records every request) and InMemoryEventBus (a validating EventSink that stores published events) — and service suites build on them with injectable collaborators: the orchestrator wires FakeSkill (scripted ok/hang/SkillError behaviors), FakeGraph and a Bus that delivers events straight to the consumer handler; the query-service injects a FakeReader (canned Cypher results, recorded queries) and a FakeOwner ASGI app standing in for the three owner services plus a cheap argon2 hasher; the extraction-agent injects a FakePlugin through serve() with a plugin_transport.

Integration tests in both languages boot real infrastructure with testcontainers — Memgraph 3.13.1 (--telemetry-enabled=false, port 7687) and NATS 2.15.0-alpine (-js, port 4222) — and skip cleanly without a Docker daemon: Python probes the Docker daemon and uses pytest.mark.skipif / pytest.skip; plain Java tests use @Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true) with Wait strategies; Quarkus-based Java tests instead use @EnabledIf with a helper that temporarily restores the Testcontainers classloader, because Quarkus replaces the thread context class loader and breaks Testcontainers' ServiceLoader lookup.

The container-backed integration tests pin the infrastructural invariants identically in both languages: the read transaction rejects writes (and nothing is created), init_schema is idempotent, RunRecorder cleanup_stale removes only facts produced by unfinished runs (marking those runs failed) while keeping facts of completed runs, the Memgraph memory-limit error is not retried (asserted to surface in under 5 seconds), and publishing the same event id twice yields exactly one delivered message and one stream message via Nats-Msg-Id deduplication.

Cross-language parity is enforced by contracts/conformance/vectors.json: the Python suite (tests/conformance/test_python_conformance.py via sandman_agent.testing.run_conformance) and the Java suite (agent-lib's ConformanceRunner via ConformanceTest) both call their own ids/Ids implementations against the same vector file and assert the returned failure list is empty, so a drift in either language fails that language's CI job; the runners deliberately do not re-implement the rules.

The skillInvocation conformance cases require a served skill and are verified per language: Python parametrizes them in libs/python/sandman-agent/tests/test_a2a.py against an in-process serve() app, and Java runs them in A2aServerTest as a @QuarkusTest test agent; the cassetteKey vectors are implemented only by the llm-replay server, which asserts the RFC 8785 canonical form and derived key in its own tests — the agent libraries deliberately do not implement cassette keys.

REST tests validate response bodies against the OpenAPI contracts at test time: the query-service's helpers.validate builds a Draft202012Validator from the operation's response schema in query-service.yaml with a referencing registry that resolves cross-file $refs into contracts/, and the orchestrator (test_rest.py) and extraction-agent (openapi_validate) do the same against their own specs — so an OpenAPI change that breaks a response fails the language test suite rather than surfacing in review.

The A2A extract plugin stub is contract-tested through the same client the extraction-agent uses: tests/plugin-stubs/tests/test_stubs.py builds the stub app and calls it with sandman_agent.A2aPluginClient over httpx.ASGITransport, pinning element/relation/explicitReference extraction of the mini fixture, DEPENDS_ON import resolution via context.currentArtifacts, non-retryable PluginError for storage paths outside, relative to, or unreadable within the artifact store, and that /healthz and the agent card are public without a token.

The plain-HTTP detect plugin stub is tested with httpx.MockTransport standing in for the query-service: the tests assert the plugin sends its own outbound bearer token with a projectId-anchored element-count Cypher query, that a queryServiceUrl hint whose origin differs from the configured query-service (SANDMAN_QUERY_SERVICE_URL) is rejected with 400 problem+json without any outbound call, that missing/wrong/non-ASCII tokens yield 401 and malformed or schema-invalid bodies yield 400 problem+json, and that a query-service failure is surfaced as 503 problem+json.

tests/e2e/test_walking_skeleton.py is skipped unless SANDMAN_E2E is set; the module-scoped stack fixture first asserts GET /readyz returns 200 at SANDMAN_E2E_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8080), then creates a per-run project and users, obtaining personal API tokens through the console: login with the bootstrap admin password (SANDMAN_E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD or the admin_bootstrap_password secret), the forced password change (SANDMAN_E2E_ADMIN_NEW_PASSWORD or the e2e_admin_password secret), and token creation — every run uses its own project and users.

The walking-skeleton e2e test drives the full analysis pipeline against tests/e2e/fixtures/mini: it ingests snapshot 1 through the real CLI (sandman_cli main) with a project member's token and asserts 6 created versions and a workflow whose steps are exactly extraction-agent/extract-artifact-versions, tlr-agent/recover-trace-links and inconsistency-agent/detect-inconsistencies, all SUCCEEDED; it then checks KG content (three requirements, MediaCache CodeUnit, run tools, explicit-reference and stub-name-match trace links, two OPEN untraced-requirement inconsistencies), triage authorization (viewer 403, stale expectedStatus 409, triager transition to DEFERRED), query read isolation (anchored query ok, unanchored 422, foreign project 403/404) and the CSV trace-link export.

The e2e test pins incremental ingestion and inconsistency lifecycle semantics: ingesting snapshot 2 (one changed file, one deleted) creates one version and deletes one artifact; re-sending the same snapshot creates/reactivates/deletes nothing and must trigger no workflow; the previously untraced requirement becomes RESOLVED with verification confirmed and a system:stub-untraced history actor; reverting to snapshot 1 reactivates two versions and moves that inconsistency to REOPENED, while the manually deferred inconsistency stays DEFERRED.

The CI workflow triggers on pushes to main, all pull requests and a nightly schedule (cron 0 3 * * *); a `changes` job (skipped on schedule) runs dorny/paths-filter and emits contracts, python, java and compose outputs, where both the python and java filters include contracts/** so the conformance vectors re-run in both language jobs whenever the shared contracts change, and the compose filter additionally covers deploy/**, config/**, tests/plugin-stubs/** and tests/e2e/**.

The CI language jobs are: `contracts` (checkout, setup-uv with Python 3.13, uv sync --locked, then uv run python scripts/validate_contracts.py), `python` (same setup, then make lint — so the guard grep, ruff and strict mypy gate the merge — and then uv run pytest), and `java` (actions/setup-java with temurin 21 and Maven caching, then mvn -B verify).

The CI compose job validates compose config with generated secrets in a temporary copy of deploy/ (running docker compose config -q for the profile combinations "" and "--profile stubs --profile obs --profile local-llm", plus the docker-compose.yml + docker-compose.dev.yml overlay), then builds and boots the stack with docker compose --profile stubs up -d --build --wait --wait-timeout 300 — the same invocation as make e2e's boot step — dumping the last 200 log lines per service on failure and always tearing down with down -v so volumes never leak.

The CI e2e job runs when the event is the nightly schedule or the compose path filter matched, with timeout-minutes 20: it checks out, sets up uv, runs uv sync --locked and then make e2e (which regenerates secrets, boots the stubs stack and runs the walking skeleton); on failure it dumps the last 300 log lines per service and it always tears down with docker compose down -v.

tests/plugin-stubs is a uv workspace member whose __main__ serves both plugin stubs in one process — the A2A extract app on port 8000 and the plain-HTTP detect app on 8001 — and its Dockerfile builds that package; the compose plugin-stubs service (profile stubs) runs exactly this image with the plugin's own outbound token and inbound plugin token as Compose secrets and a read-only artifact-store mount, which is what make e2e and the CI compose/e2e jobs boot.

The root pyproject pins the Python test toolchain in the dev dependency group (ruff, mypy, pytest, pytest-asyncio, testcontainers, plus type stubs) and defines a separate `contracts` dependency group (jsonschema, referencing, rfc8785, openapi-spec-validator, pyyaml) that dev includes, so contract validation can be run with `uv sync --group contracts` without any test tooling; the uv workspace members cover libs/python/*, the Python services, tools/cli and tests/plugin-stubs.
